title: Sliding window
summary: Keep a running total instead of re-adding everything.

cards.title: The question
cards.body:
A player's scores over 8 rounds: `2 1 5 1 3 2 9 1`. What's the best total over any **3 rounds in a row**?

The slow way adds up every group of 3 from scratch. With window size k that's about **n × k** additions.

cards.title: Slide, don't restart
cards.body:
When the window moves one step right, only two things change: one value **enters**, one value **leaves**.

So: `sum = sum + entering - leaving`. One addition and one subtraction per step, which is **O(n)** total.

cards.title: In games
cards.body: Sliding windows are everywhere in real-time code: an FPS counter averaged over the last 60 frames, detecting a "hot streak" in recent spins, smoothing analogue stick input.

cards.question: Window size 4 over 1,000 values. Roughly how many additions does the sliding version make?
cards.explain: 4 to build the first window, then one add and one subtract per step: about 1,000 steps. The naive way is about 4,000.

cards.title: Build it: count good windows
cards.body: Count windows of size k whose sum is at least a target. Same slide, plus one `if`.
